name: decision_agent
functionality: Final orchestrator - evaluates all upstream agent outputs via a deterministic decision tree to produce the return recommendation. Three separate prompt variants: (1) DAMAGED_PRODUCT prompt with 6-Step evaluation (CX vs OBD first -> Intent Resonance -> OBD -> CX -> CX vs OBD recheck -> Risk Signals) with 8 rules and 40+ path examples, (2) MISSHIPMENT prompt with similar 6-Step flow but different logic paths for misshipment cases, (3) REMAINING REASON prompt (v4.0) with 9 sequential rules covering all other return reasons.
inputs: return_id, order_id, hyperlocal_customer_profile, cx_universal_trust_sub_profile, return_reason, return_sub_reason, ri_flag, agent_findings (outputs from all 8 upstream agents: context_agent, intent_resonance_agent, catalog_correctness_agent, image_adjudication_obd_agent, image_adjudication_cx_agent, image_adjudication_cx_vs_obd_agent, image_adjudication_cx_vs_pod_agent, risk_signals_agent), plus rvp metrics
inputType: Text (JSON - aggregated outputs from all other agents + order metadata)
promptDescription: 3 prompt variants: (1) DAMAGED_PRODUCT Decision Agent - 6-Step strict flow: Step 1 eval cx_vs_obd (Damage/Misshipment -> Reject STOP), Step 2 eval intent_resonance, Step 3 eval obd_agent, Step 4 eval cx_agent, Step 5 recheck cx_vs_obd, Step 6 eval risk_signals. 8 rules + 40+ path examples. (2) MISSHIPMENT Decision Agent - Same 6-Step structure but different logic for misshipment-specific paths (e.g., OBD Can't Say + CX Misshipment -> after risk -> Approve). (3) REMAINING REASON (v4.0, Author: raghavendra.b, Updated: 2026-02-05) - 9 sequential rules: 1.Catalog Issue->Approve, 2.Intent Issue->DI, 3.OBD confirms problem->Approve, 4.High Risk->Reject, 5.OBD missing+CX confirms->Approve, 6.OBD No Issue->Reject, 7.CX No Issue->Reject, 8.Both lack product_match->DI, 9.Fallback->DI.
promptVersions: DAMAGED_PRODUCT variant, MISSHIPMENT variant, REMAINING_REASON v4.0
